Smt. Madubala vs Suresh on 6 August, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:21007
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 6 th Of August, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 7544 of 2023
 Smt. Madubala And Others
 Versus
 Suresh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Chandra Prakash Purohit, learned counsel for the
Shri Bhaskar Agrawal, Advocate with Shri Pradip Kumar

learned counsel for respondent No.3.
 Order

The appellants have filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 21.08.2023 in MACC No.01/2019 on the question of quantum of compensation.
2. The liability of the Insurance Company and the death due to the accident are not in dispute.
3. The brief facts of the case are that on 15.11.2018 at around 08.30 PM, the deceased along with his brother Radheshyam was going on his motorcycle from his Village to visit relatives in Negrun.
When they reached near Maukhandi Fante, respondent No.1 riding a motorcycle bearing registration number MP-13-ES-8545, in a rash and negligent manner, rammed into the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result, the deceased sustained grievous injuries to various parts of his body.
Consequently, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21007 2 MA-7544-2023 deceased ultimately died on 17.01.2019 due to the injuries sustained.

3.1. The appellants / claimants filed their claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 before the Claims Tribunal for the death of the Gopal in the aforesaid accident claiming compensation.
The Claims Tribunal, after considering the evidence on record, concluded that an amount of Rs.9,52,000/- would be appropriate compensation for the loss of dependency.
After awarding the compensation under other heads, a total sum of Rs.13,93,491/- was awarded.
4. Counsel for the appellants submits that the Claims Tribunal has not correctly assessed the income of the deceased.
He further submits that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month as he was involved in agriculture as well as working as a driver.

The Claims Tribunal, after considering this Smt. Madubala vs Suresh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86495194/
1 claim, concluded that there was no material to rely on this assertion regarding the income of the deceased.

sentences.text: The Tribunal, therefore, observed that, based on guesswork, the income was taken at Rs.5,000/- per month.
Counsel for the appellants submits that guesswork cannot be a basis for assessment of income, there must be some reference material for determining the income, even on a national basis.
He further submit that no amount has been awarded for loss of consortium to the daughter and son of the deceased.
He, therefore, prays for the enhancement of compensation accordingly.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 / Insurance Company referring to the findings of the Claims Tribunal in para 31 submits that it has clearly been recorded by the Claims Tribunal that there was no NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21007 3 MA-7544-2023 material available to establish the income of the deceased.
Therefore, in light of this, the income at Rs.5,000/- per month has been correctly taken on a national basis.
He, thus, supports the findings of the award and prays for the dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
7.

It is seen from para 31 of the impugned award that the Claims Tribunal while disbelieving the claim of income at Rs.20,000/- per month has not based its conclusion on any reference material but merely on guesswork.
A figure of Rs.5000/- was taken, which is not a proper way for determining income on a national basis.
There should have been some reference material for ascertaining the minimum wages for an unskilled labourer at the relevant time.

8. It is noted that as per the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority at the relevant time i.e. on the date of accident (15/11/2018), the minimum wages for an unskilled labourer was Rs.7,300/- per month.
Thus, the income of the deceased is taken at Rs.7,300/- per month.

9. As regards the amount of consortium, the claim of the learned counsel for the appellant appears to be correct in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram reported in 2019 ACJ SC 2782 .

sentences.text: Both the son and the daughter are entitled to compensation for the loss of parental consortium, which amounts to Rs.88,000/-.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21007 4 MA-7544-2023 10.
As such, the compensation for loss of dependency would now be changed to Rs.13,89,920/- and the total amount of compensation would come to Rs.19,19,411/-.

11. The Claims Tribunal has already awarded an amount of Rs.13,93,491/-, thus, the appellants are now entitled to the payment of Rs.5,25,920/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
12. The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the application before the Claims Tribunal.
